key_insight: GRC reframes learning as recursively closing residual gaps while preserving both prior responsibilities and the ability to learn new ones.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a principled update rule for stable yet plastic models, relevant to adaptive simulation, control, and constitutive-style learning systems that must avoid catastrophic regression.
method: Defines two primitive learning modes: transformation within a representation and revision of the representation itself.
Derives a local tangent decomposition and a criterion for when representation revision is necessary.
Proves an affine-case stability-plasticity condition and a unique constrained quadratic update that safely reduces residuals while preserving old responsibilities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results, including necessary-and-sufficient conditions, uniqueness of the update solution, and proof-based comparisons, rather than empirical dataset evaluation.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on regularity assumptions and an affine formulation, so practical performance may depend on how closely a target system matches those conditions.
paper_title: Generalized Residual Closure: General Learning Dynamics for Stability-Plasticity Compatibility
